open_questions.question: Exact first-edition publication month/day in 1983. Wikipedia and turing.org.uk give the year only; October or November 1983 is mentioned in passing but no primary source directly fetched.
open_questions.proposed_route: Fetch the British Library catalogue entry or the original UK publisher's records for the exact publication date of the Burnett Books/Hutchinson edition.

open_questions.question: Did 'Alan Turing: The Enigma' win the Premio Giovanni Comisso in 1992? turing.org.uk lists this, but the Premio Comisso website's 1992 winners list does not appear to name Hodges. The claim may refer to the Italian translation ('Alan Turing, Storia di un Enigma', Bollati Boringhieri) rather than the English original.
open_questions.proposed_route: Fetch the Premio Comisso winners page directly (premiocomisso.it/i-vincitori/) and cross-check against the year 1992 and the Italian edition publication date.

open_questions.question: First-edition UK page count: 587 or 576? Wikipedia says 587; some bookseller records say 576. These could reflect the same printing with/without front matter counted differently.
open_questions.proposed_route: Fetch the British Library catalogue record (bl.uk) or Internet Archive scan for the 1983 Burnett Books first edition to read the physical page count.

open_questions.question: Does the Turing-test conceptual lineage (alan-turing -> conceptual-ancestor-of -> claude) pass through this book as a relay node? Hodges documents Turing's 1950 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' paper in the biography. No source directly attests the book as a relay in the lineage, so this is not a fact-backed edge.

candidate_edge.verification_route: Find a source explicitly citing the Hodges biography as having influenced AI researchers at Anthropic, or any primary Anthropic/Claude model card citing it.

open_questions.proposed_route: Search Anthropic research papers or Claude model cards for any citation of Hodges or the Turing biography.

open_questions.question: Are there formal awards beyond the Guardian list (2002) and NY Times bestseller (2014)? turing.org.uk mentions the Premio Comisso claim (disputed above) and 'New Statesman Ten Essential Books on Technology (2009)'. The 2009 New Statesman claim was not directly fetched.
open_questions.proposed_route: Fetch the New Statesman 2009 article directly or search their archive for the technology books list.
